dedupe_keys.name: aceee white paper energy efficiency and demand flexibility to reduce data centre energy use and peak demand 2025

description: This ACEEE white paper by Steven Nadel, dated October 2025, reviews opportunities to use energy efficiency and demand flexibility to reduce data centre energy use and peak demand in the United States. It describes data centre types (hyperscale, colocation, enterprise and edge, with an estimate of the server share by type), shows an illustrative split of energy use of about 80 percent for IT equipment, 15 percent for cooling and 5 percent for electrical equipment and lighting at a PUE of 1.25, and summarises efficiency opportunities in servers and chips, software and algorithms, cooling and heat recovery, with an appendix that discusses them in more detail. Producer: ACEEE, a nonprofit research organisation, supported by the Tilia Fund and reviewed by outside experts. Coverage: the US, with global chip efficiency trends. Access: a free 34-page PDF on the ACEEE website. Licence and cost: ACEEE's terms say citation is welcome but certain uses need prior written permission and for-profit uses may incur a fee; free to read. Caveats: the paper reviews published estimates and does not provide a downloadable dataset, and the demand flexibility sections were not read in full. Simulation uses: the efficiency shares and flexibility options give assumptions for data centre load, capacity-planning and optimisation models. Related records: the EPRI DCFlex tariff and survey dataset (data-epri-dcflex-flexible-load-tariffs-and-survey) and the IEA 4E critical review of data centre energy use (data-iea-4e-data-centre-energy-use-critical-review).
